title: The Library
strapline: Shh — choose your book, take it to the desk, and hear the satisfying stamp that means it's yours to take home.
intent: The library is where a lifelong love of books can begin, and playing at running one — and knowing a real one exists in the community — puts children at the heart of a world of stories.
The librarian is a gentle, welcoming community helper, and the role play builds knowledge of the people and places that share books and learning with everyone for free.
Choosing, sorting, shelving and stamping books weaves in mathematics — matching, ordering, categorising, counting, and caring for a system.
Borrowing, returning and looking after books grows responsibility, turn-taking and respect for shared things.
The library is soaked in literacy — reading, sharing and talking about books, and the mark-making of tickets, stamps and library cards.
Vocabulary and knowledge grow — library, borrow, return, author, shelf, quiet, member, share.
implementation: Set up a library corner — a good range of books, a stamp and date pad, library cards, a returns box, a cosy reading nook and a librarian's desk.
Take a reader's role so children help you find, choose, issue and return books: 'I'm looking for a book about dinosaurs — can you help me find one?'
Model the librarian's welcoming, quiet talk and the care of books — how we turn pages, why we keep our voices low, when the book is due back.
Bring in maths through the play — sort books by size, colour or topic, shelve them in order, stamp and count the borrowings, match cards to members.
Fill the play with real literacy — sharing and talking about stories, writing library cards and tickets, recommending favourites to friends.
Link to the real world — visit or talk about your local library, run a story time, and let children take the responsibility of the returns and reminders.
key_questions: I'm looking for a book about dinosaurs — can you help me find one?
How shall we sort these books — by size, colour or topic?
When is this book due back?
How many books have we stamped out today?
Which book would you recommend to a friend?
